lesson.title: Comparing Functions
intro: Functions can be compared using graphs, equations, and tables.
A y-intercept is the value of a function when \(x=0\).
To compare rates of change or intercepts, use the representation that is given and evaluate carefully.

questions.prompt: Which graph below represents a function that is always decreasing over the entire interval \(-3 < x < 3\)?
questions.explanation: Only choice 4 is decreasing for every \(x\) in the interval \(-3 < x < 3\).

questions.prompt: Three functions are given below. Which functions have the same y-intercept?
choices: The functions all have different y-intercepts.
questions.explanation: Evaluate each function at \(x=0\). \(f(0)=-|0+2|+7=5\), \(g(0)=(0-3)^2-4=5\), and from the table \(h(0)=-3\). Therefore, \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) have the same y-intercept.
